title: Kernel Groove — weekly cadence and runbook sketch
content:
Meeting: weekly engineering sync — Kernel Groove
Date: 2029-09-11 (Wed) 10:00-10:50 PT
Participants: Ava Chen (host), Diego Morales, Priya Nair, Liam O'Connor, Rashmi Patel, plus oncall drop-ins

Purpose: short standup + experimental checkins for kernel-level prefill + KV-cache coordination and batching heuristics. Focus this week: stabilizing the new microkernel cooperative yield and confirming rollback criteria for canary traffic.

Summary (top lines)
- Microkernel cooperative yield merged to canary; currently running on 10% of traffic in us-west1 dedicated pool. Latency tail looks stable but we see a 3-4% increase in p95 under heavy multi-tenant tails.
- KV prefill coalescer A/B experiment started (A: current coalescer, B: compact-window coalescer). Early signal: B reduces cold-cache misses by ~12% but increases end-to-end median latency for short prompts by 6ms.
- Batching heuristic: added early-exit for sequences shorter than 64 tokens in the client router; feature flag rolling out to dev and staging for 48 hours before prod.

Notes and logs
- Diego: kernel micro-yield merge notes
  - PR: #2147 merged to canary branch at 02:35 UTC. Added cooperative sleep of 50us when KV hotset contention detects >3 concurrent writers.
  - Observed behavior: throughput unchanged at p50 but p99 spikes when write-thrashing occurs on a single GPU slice. Hypothesis: contention shifting IO waits into scheduler; need to instrument kernel->runtime handoff for the slice.
  - Action: Diego to add per-slice contention meter (prom counter) and a histogram for kernel-sleep durations by slice. ETA: 2029-09-13.

- Priya: KV prefill coalescer experiment status
  - Experiment started 2029-09-10 00:00 UTC. Traffic routed through experiments service: 50k requests sample/day.
  - Metrics after 24h: cold-cache miss rate (A=0.18, B=0.158), avg token cost savings B ~ -4% on cached traces, median latency short prompts (A=26ms, B=32ms).
  - Unresolved: why median latency increased — likely extra work in coalescer path for small sequences. Looking at micro-profiling traces next.
  - Action: Priya to run flamegraph for coalescer code path on 2029-09-12 and propose a small refactor to early-bail for sequences < 16 tokens.

- Liam: Batching heuristic rollouts and client router change log
  - Implemented early-exit for router batching when queue contains >80% requests with sequence_len < 64. Feature gated under FLAG:router.batch.shortseq_early_exit.
  - Staging rollout passed 12h soak. Dev cluster observed ~2% improved throughput for mixed workloads.
  - Risk: may reduce batching for medium-length prompts leading to higher per-token cost; will monitor cost dashboard and set autoscaler thresholds if needed.
  - Action: Liam to add a dashboard tile tracking batch size distribution and to set alert if mean batch size falls by >10% in 1h. ETA: 2029-09-12.

- Rashmi: oncall notes + fallback policy verification
  - Incident simulated: kernel prefill worker OOM on canary at 2029-09-10 19:04 UTC. Canary fallback correctly routed traffic to baseline model variant; however, traces show increased latency during re-route.
  - Findings: re-route adds ~120ms due to cache warmup; potential user visible blips for chat flows.
  - Proposal: add a soft-warmup path that serves from a warm shadow cache for first 5s post-fallback to reduce tail.
  - Action: Rashmi to draft RFC for soft-warmup and run tabletop with SRE/Platform on 2029-09-14.

Decisions made
- Keep microkernel yield in canary for one more week; collect per-slice metrics then decide on widening to 30% or revert.
- Continue KV coalescer A/B for an additional 72h; if cold-cache miss delta remains >=10% while median latency penalty <10%, consider promoting B to default behind a short-sequence bail-out.
- Router batching early-exit to be promoted to prod after 48h full prod-canary soak and no regression in scheduling fairness metrics.

Action items (owners + ETA)
- Diego Morales: add per-slice contention meters and kernel-sleep histograms; instrument and push metrics to grafana. ETA 2029-09-13.
- Priya Nair: flamegraph coalescer trace + PR for early-bail for <16 token sequences. ETA 2029-09-12.
- Liam O'Connor: create batch-size-distribution dashboard tile and alert; confirm FLAG rollout plan for prod. ETA 2029-09-12.
- Rashmi Patel: draft soft-warmup RFC and schedule tabletop run with SRE. ETA 2029-09-14.
- Ava Chen: compile weekly summary for eng sync and send to product/console leads. ETA 2029-09-13.

Open questions / parking lot
- Should we consider splitting coalescer paths by request size at the routing layer (i.e., route tiny sequences to a low-latency coalescer)? Tradeoffs: extra routing complexity vs potential latency wins.
- Do we need a per-customer KV cache sizing heuristic? Large customers currently dominate hotset causing noisy eviction for smaller tenants.
- Long-term: if microkernel yield is good, can we convert fixed sleep into adaptive backoff based on measured contention percentile?

Quick wins / experiment ideas
- Short-sequence fast-path in coalescer (Priya).
- Adaptive cooperative yield: dynamic sleep tuned by 95th percentile contention (Diego + Liam).
- Client-side opt-in to prefer cached routes for known warm-session flows.

Notes to self / rough TODOs (Ava)
- Add ENG-7839 to prioritize per-customer hotset diagnostics.
- Follow up with Console team about showing canary region flag in rollout UI.
- Remind infra to reserve extra dev GPUs for heavier flamegraph runs on 2029-09-12.

Standup blips (two-liners from each attendee)
- Ava: will draft weekly note.
- Diego: adding instrumentation today.
- Priya: perf traces tomorrow.
- Liam: dashboard + alerting.
- Rashmi: RFC + tabletop scheduling.

Appendix (short logs and links)
- Canary cluster: us-west1-dedicated-pool-canary (10% traffic)
- Kernel PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2147
- Coalescer A/B experiment sheet: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRV/kv-prefill-experiments
- Incident replay: ENG-7802 (oom simulation)

End of notes.
